clue.text: Vicissitudes – of a rollercoaster ride?

definitions.note: a description of the ride's motion rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: changes of fortune, good and bad in turn
second meaning: the literal climbs and plunges of the track

explanation.surface: A dramatic word for life's changes, likened to the thrills of a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits the clue in two: a formal word, then a playful literal picture of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicissitudes are alternating spells of good and bad fortune, which the idiom describes as rising and falling.

clue.text: Result of flipping ungainly drop?

blocks.note: surface reading: tossing a flapjack in a frying pan and watching where it comes down
setter's reading: an aircraft coming down flat and heavily, belly first

explanation.walkthrough: Flipping suggests Shrove Tuesday cookery; the answer is an aviation term for a clumsy flat touchdown, which is also literally what a tossed batter disc does.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane that drops flat onto the runway without proper glide makes this kind of clumsy, heavy arrival.

clue.text: Fever indistinct, brow wiped

indicators.note: the brow is the top of a face, so in a down entry the topmost letter is wiped away

blocks.note: something indistinct is vague

explanation.surface: A feverish patient, hazy-minded, has their forehead mopped.
explanation.walkthrough: Brow wiped in a down clue means the first letter goes: VAGUE loses its V.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is an old word for a malarial fever with shivering fits, so it is a kind of fever.

clue.text: Sparkler in a tin made to shake

indicators.note: shaking jumbles the contents of a container, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firework sparkler kept in a tin that someone shakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sparkler suggests a firework, but it is costume jewellery; the fodder is A TIN MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is glittering fake-gem decoration on clothing, something that sparkles like cut stones.

clue.text: Birth at home after transfer set up

indicators.note: in a down entry, setting something up raises it so it reads from the bottom upward
one piece follows another, so it is written second in the entry

blocks.note: a giro is a bank transfer of money, common in Britain
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A baby arrives at home after the mother is moved.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro is a British system of bank transfer, a word less familiar outside the UK; in a down clue, set up means read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth and this word both mean the beginning or source from which something comes into existence.

clue.text: Shaved piece, close

indicators.note: shaving trims away from the edges, so letters at both ends are removed

blocks.note: a knight is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A slice has been shaved off, and it was a close shave.
explanation.walkthrough: Piece here is a chess piece, the KNIGHT; lose its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old-fashioned word for near, so it means physically or temporally close.

clue.text: Average boy after song enters playing instrument

indicators.note: one piece follows the other, so it is written second
something that enters goes inside, so this pair sits within the outer word

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
Tom is a boy's name
playing a fiddle is fiddling

explanation.surface: An average lad follows a song by joining in on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Playing instrument looks like a description of the boy; it is one word, a fiddle being played, and the song-plus-boy pair sits inside it after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something moderately good, neither excellent nor poor, just middling quality.

clue.text: Bend clearly awkward for manipulator of abs

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsily arranged, so the letters are set out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gym instruction: this stomach bend is clearly awkward for someone working their abdominal muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: The manipulator of abs sounds like a fitness trainer, but it is a performer whose dance works the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer's dance style is built on rippling and isolating the stomach muscles, so she controls her abdominals.

clue.text: Various lines with a tag put in binder

indicators.note: various suggests mixed or assorted forms, so the letters take a different arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Assorted lines with a label slipped into a ring binder folder.
explanation.walkthrough: Binder suggests a stationery folder; it is something that wraps and binds electrical wires.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricians wrap this sticky plastic strip around wires and joints, binding them together safely.

clue.text: Money I say remains on the table?

blocks.note: bread is slang for money
Crumbs! is a dated British exclamation of surprise, like 'I say!'

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that money has been left lying on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: I say reads as speech but it is an exclamation to be replaced by an equivalent one.
explanation.definitionFit: After a meal, the little scraps of loaf left scattered across the dining surface are what remain.

clue.text: Horse tethered by caballero, a nag

indicators.note: what is tethered is held fast by the words around it, so the letters sit inside them

blocks.note: the end of the Spanish word, then the article, then the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A Spanish horseman has tied up his tired old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A caballero is a Spanish gentleman or horseman, which makes the setting fit the horse definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse whose coat mixes white hairs with a darker colour.

clue.text: Legally binding, almost everything in film

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped
one thing placed in another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: vid is short for video, a film
everything is all

explanation.surface: A contract is binding for nearly everything shown in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Vid is informal shorthand for a video, so it can stand for a film; almost applies only to the word right after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A valid contract or document has legal force and can be upheld in court.

clue.text: Test of reading ancient literature, originally

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: An exam on reading old classic texts.
explanation.walkthrough: Ancient literature was originally passed on by mouth, a neat nod to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a test answered by talking rather than writing.

clue.text: Odd letters only, and man goes for proverb

indicators.note: odd positions are the first, third, fifth and so on, so only those are kept

blocks.note: letters one, three, five, seven and nine

explanation.surface: A saying about a man who only reads odd letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection runs straight across word breaks: a-n-d-m-a-n-g-o-e-s.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional saying expressing a general truth, which is exactly a proverb.

clue.text: Five entertained by dance party

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five guests are entertained by a dancing party.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A revel is a lively, noisy celebration, a party with much merrymaking.

clue.text: Story one acted out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, as a bone put out of joint, so the letters change places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tale that a single performer dramatised.
explanation.walkthrough: Acted out reads as a phrasal verb; only out is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing account of a real incident, a type of story.

clue.text: Note – one’s played

definitions.note: a phrase describing the thing rather than a single synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: write down, as a verb
second meaning: a vinyl disc put on a turntable

explanation.surface: A musical note, and one that's being played.
explanation.walkthrough: Note looks musical; it is the verb to jot down.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to write it down; a vinyl disc is spun on a turntable for music.

clue.text: Escallop cooked in crumble

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A scallop baked into a crumble dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: An escallop is a scallop; crumble looks like a pudding but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumble is to fall apart or give way, as a building does when it falls down.

clue.text: Storm – is that electrical?

definitions.note: a question hinting at a property of electricity rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: rush forward in attack
second meaning: the property carried by electrons and ions

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a thunderstorm is caused by electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: Storm is a verb, as troops storm a position.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who storm a position rush at it in attack; electrical particles carry positive or negative electricity.

clue.text: A demonic, warped entertainer

indicators.note: something warped is bent out of shape, so the letters lose their original order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer with a dark, twisted sense of humour.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the fodder from its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian performs jokes to amuse audiences, a kind of stage or screen performer.

clue.text: Bird surviving wife, both with wings clipped

indicators.note: clipping a bird's wings trims each side, so the outermost letters are cut off

blocks.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII and the one who outlived him
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird outlives its mate, and both have had their flight feathers clipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Both is fodder as well as sounding like the signal's scope: BOTH loses B and H. Henry VIII's wives ran divorced, beheaded, died, divorced, beheaded, survived.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a brightly coloured tropical bird that can mimic speech.

clue.text: Tongue rolling over universal medicine briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes
rolling over turns something end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: U is the film certificate for universal
a drug is a medicine

explanation.surface: A tongue rolls over a cure-all pill for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal medicine looks like a panacea; the words work separately. DRUG shortens to DRU.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue here means language; Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also spoken in India.

clue.text: Agree with friend on conclusion of project

indicators.note: a conclusion is the end, so the final letter is kept
in an across entry, placing one thing on another sets it after it

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Coming to terms with a colleague at the end of a project.
explanation.walkthrough: Agree with reads as one phrase, but with is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tally correspond or match each other, so the verb means to be consistent.

clue.text: Lip bitten by worried gentleman

indicators.note: something bitten is gripped between teeth, so the letters are held inside the neighbouring words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An anxious man chewing his lip.
explanation.walkthrough: Lip is the brim of a cup, not the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The lip of a cup or cliff is its rim, the outer boundary or brink.

clue.text: Joint leader in kart, even after taking a spin

indicators.note: the leader is at the front, so only the opening letter is taken
a spin turns something round, so the letters face the other way
one piece follows another, so it is written second

blocks.note: the opening letter
e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Joint first place in a go-kart race, even after spinning off.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint leader reads as a shared lead; joint is the definition. E'en is poetic for even.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint in the middle of the leg.

clue.text: Article though for neighbour

definitions.note: a verb here, to lie next to

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
but and though both introduce a contrast

explanation.surface: A newspaper item, though, written for the person next door.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbour looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to border.
explanation.definitionFit: Two properties that neighbour each other share a boundary and touch along it.

clue.text: Unstable nation, something of a split country?

definitions.note: a whimsical description, the split being a dessert

blocks.note: first meaning: a politically volatile small state dependent on one export
second meaning: a country made of the fruit in a banana split sundae

explanation.surface: A shaky country divided against itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Split suggests a divided nation; it is the ice-cream dessert, whose main fruit names the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a small corrupt state with shaky government, often reliant on exporting a single crop.

clue.text: Spotlight something to spend on the theatre

blocks.note: a cent is a coin you can spend
re means on or concerning
the stage is the acting profession, the theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre spending money on its lighting rig.
explanation.walkthrough: On here is RE, the business-letter word for concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the spotlight means being the focus of attention, the most prominent position in view.
